title: Closing the yield gap in Sub-Saharan Africa
bottleneck: African maize yields lag far behind what's agronomically possible — raising gains to a modest 80 kg/ha/year, already achieved in harsh US environments, would boost production 53% in a decade — but the gap persists due to broken seed systems, fertilizer access, extension services, and worsening soil degradation. The constraint isn't knowing what's needed but delivery: inputs, credit, and knowledge don't reach smallholders.
why_it_blocks: The region with the fastest population growth holds the largest untapped yield potential. Failing to close the gap means rising imports, hunger, and cropland expansion.
current_state: Targeted programs show gains are possible, but adoption of improved practices remains low and FAO assessments show soil degradation worsening across most regions. A few national programs show gains are possible, but extension reach remains a fraction of what is needed.
